problem_summary.summary: Check whether a string reads identically in both directions after ignoring non-alphanumeric characters and letter case.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a printable-ASCII string s. Return true if the normalized sequence is a palindrome, otherwise false.
constraints: s consists only of printable ASCII characters

brute_force.explanation: Build a normalized string containing only lowercase letters and digits, then compare it with its reverse.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Normalization applies exactly the requested filtering and case folding. A sequence is a palindrome precisely when its forward form equals its reversed form.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — normalization and reversal each scan the string.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary — the normalized characters are stored separately.

optimized.explanation: Place pointers at both ends, skip non-alphanumeric characters, and compare lowercase forms while the pointers move inward.
optimized.correctness_idea: Every compared pair is the next pair of relevant characters from opposite ends of the normalized sequence. Any unequal pair disproves a palindrome; if all pairs match, the sequence is symmetric.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each pointer moves inward across the string at most once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — only two indices and character temporaries are used.

steps.condition: Both endpoint characters are alphanumeric and their lowercase forms match.

steps.event: Skip punctuation at both sides and compare the middle letter.
steps.condition: Comma, space, and exclamation mark are skipped; the remaining characters match.
steps.action: Advance both pointers; they cross and the scan succeeds.

edge_cases.handling: No relevant characters remain, so the empty normalized sequence is a palindrome.
The pointers meet without finding a mismatched pair.

edge_cases.case: Digits are part of the comparison
edge_cases.handling: Digits are retained and compared like letters.
